about.title: Avalon Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Avalon has its own rhythm. A small town of about 3,800 people sees deliveries threading through a compact street grid, hospitality staff stretching to cover busy weekends, and maintenance crews handling everything from hillside properties to waterfront equipment. When one of those jobs leads to an injury, the practical question comes first: who pays for the doctor and the missed paychecks? Under California law, workers' compensation normally covers medical care and part of your wages regardless of who was at fault, and it is generally your only claim against your employer. Many job injuries, though, involve someone else entirely. A subcontractor leaves a hazard, a tool fails, a property owner skips a repair, or another driver strikes your work vehicle. Avalon recorded 11 injury collisions in 2025, with 17 people hurt and no traffic deaths, and public records list Wrigley Terrace Road, Wrigley Road, Marilla Avenue, and Saint Catherine Way among the streets with the most reported crashes. If a third party contributed to your injury, a separate claim may run alongside workers' comp. LawProactive connects Avalon workers with an independent attorney, free of charge, to sort out which path fits.

whyChoose.title: Why Avalon Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Two Claims Can Exist Side by Side
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or driver may face a separate injury claim. An attorney can check whether both apply to you.

items.title: Deadlines Are Easy to Miss
items.desc: You should report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party claim generally carries a two-year filing window. Getting connected early keeps both clocks in view.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: California prohibits employers from punishing you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you have been demoted, cut from the schedule, or let go after getting hurt, that is worth raising with an attorney.

items.question: I was hit by another driver on Wrigley Road while making deliveries for my job. Do I have to pick between workers' comp and a lawsuit?
items.answer: No. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and a portion of lost wages regardless of fault. Because a separate driver caused the crash, you may also have a third-party claim against that driver for losses workers' comp does not pay. An attorney can coordinate the two so one does not undercut the other.

items.question: I only work in Avalon during the busy season. Am I still covered if I get hurt?
items.answer: Seasonal, part-time, and temporary employees are generally covered by workers' compensation in California just like year-round staff. What matters is that you were an employee performing work when the injury happened, not how many months you are on the payroll. Report the injury to your employer promptly, ideally in writing, within the 30-day window.

items.question: Does LawProactive cost anything, and are you a law firm?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm and charges you nothing. We connect injured Avalon workers with an independent personal injury attorney who reviews the situation and explains the options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
